newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian court jails ex-governor for graft.
newsitem.headline: Algerian court jails ex-governor for graft.

text.p: An Algerian court on Wednesday sentenced a former provincial governor to one year in jail for graft and passed prison sentences on six other defendants, the official Algerian news agency APS said.

The court in Tizi-Ouzou, 90 km (60 miles) east of Algiers, also jailed Nourredine Lakhdar Benacer for a year and fined him 5,000 dinars ($89) for offences including "trading "marketing sate-owned assets" while in office, APS said.
Five other defendants also received one year jail terms. A seventh, who was not present in court, was sentenced to five years in prison, APS said.

Benacer was sacked in 1995 from his job as governor of Bouira, 90 km (60 miles) southeast of Algiers. He is the most senior official sentenced to jail by a criminal court for graft since President Liamine Zeroual pledged last year to crack down on corruption.
